heading: Economic growth over the very long run
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 1 with every country (region menu and legend), scale buttons and a range slider
plot_title: U.K. GDP per person in 2022 was 33 times its level in the year 1
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: [Maddison Project Database 2023, GDP per capita (`gdppc`) and population, Groningen Growth and Development Centre](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/historicaldevelopment/maddison/releases/maddison-project-database-2023)
(Bolt and van Zanden 2024, [doi:10.34894/INZBF2](https://doi.org/10.34894/INZBF2));
for the earliest years of the textbook's six countries, Angus Maddison's own estimates, the

Prepared files: [`data/ch03/fig3-1.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch03/fig3-1.csv) and [`data/ch03/maddison_longrun.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch03/maddison_longrun.csv)
(see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch03/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 3.1 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

heading: Per capita GDP in the United States
cell_title: Website version: Fig. 2 with every country of the Maddison Project (region menu and legend)
plot_title: U.S. GDP per person grew about 18-fold from 1870 to 2025
source_note:
**Sources.** Data: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED: [real GDP (`GDPCA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDPCA), [population (`B230RC0A052NBEA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/B230RC0A052NBEA)
and [GDP deflator (`A191RD3A086NBEA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/A191RD3A086NBEA), from 1929;
before 1929 and for every other country: [Maddison Project Database 2023, GDP per capita (`gdppc`) and population, Groningen Growth and Development Centre](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/historicaldevelopment/maddison/releases/maddison-project-database-2023)
(Bolt and van Zanden 2024, [doi:10.34894/INZBF2](https://doi.org/10.34894/INZBF2))
(the textbook uses the Barro-Ursúa data before 1929).
Prepared files: [`data/ch03/fig3-2.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch03/fig3-2.csv) and [`data/ch03/maddison_world.csv`](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch03/maddison_world.csv)
(see the [data notes](https://github.com/quarcs-lab/macro102-site/blob/main/data/ch03/README.md)).
Chart: inspired by Fig. 3.2 in Jones (2024), [*Macroeconomics*, 6th ed.](https://wwnorton.com/books/9781324063612)

source_note:
**Sources.** Data: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED: [real GDP (`GDPCA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDPCA), [population (`B230RC0A052NBEA`)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/B230RC0A052NBEA)
